spec.description: Cancels one or more open orders in a single request, identified by a range of client or Kraken identifiers. The details of each cancelled order are also streamed on the `executions` channel.

request.title: CancelOrderParams
request.description: Parameters identifying one or more open orders to cancel. Exactly one of `order_id`, `cl_ord_id`, `order_userref` should be supplied -- they cannot be combined in the same request.

order_id.description: Kraken `order_id` identifiers to cancel. Cannot be combined with `cl_ord_id` or `order_userref` in the same request.

cl_ord_id.description: Client `cl_ord_id` identifiers to cancel. Cannot be combined with `order_id` or `order_userref` in the same request.

order_userref.description: Client `order_userref` identifiers to cancel. Cannot be combined with `order_id` or `cl_ord_id` in the same request.

order_id.description: Kraken identifier of the cancelled order.

cl_ord_id.description: Client identifier of the cancelled order, if any.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings about the cancellation, if any.

notes: `token` (the auth bearer token) is documented by Kraken as a required params field but is deliberately absent from this schema: `core/transport/ws.py`'s `SocketConnection.rpc_send` merges the cached token into every outgoing `params` on the private connection -- trading calls and subscribe/unsubscribe alike -- so it is transport-injected, never a caller-supplied argument, the same way `req_id` (the declared `correlate` field) never appears in a requestBody schema. Exactly one of `order_id`/`cl_ord_id`/`order_userref` should be supplied; none is declared JSON Schema `required` since this is a mutual-exclusivity business rule over independently-optional array fields, documented in each field's description instead (an `anyOf` would misrepresent it as a shape union, which it isn't). Separately: the doc page states "When cancelling multiple orders, there will be a stream of individual order responses" -- i.e. cancelling N orders in one `cancel_order` call appears to answer with N reply frames sharing one `req_id`, not one aggregate reply. `responses.reply` here describes a single such frame (`CancelOrderResult`); this is a real mismatch against the format's "one command, one answering frame" model and against `WsRpcClient.request`'s single-`await`-single-reply implementation (`core/transport/ws.py`) -- flagging for review, not resolving here, since nothing in this pass touches `pkg/`.
